earlier_scan.source_named: Lissarrague, Amanda 2007. Dhanggati grammar and dictionary. Muurrbay Aboriginal Language and Culture Co-operative. Also Lissarrague 2000, A salvage grammar of Dunghutti.
earlier_scan.note: Two grammar sketches by Lissarrague plausibly state stress; no open-access copy found (Wikipedia article has no stress section).

sources.citation: Marcussen, Lisa (comp.). 2015. Selected bibliography of material on Dhanggatti / Daingatti / Dunghutti language and people held in the AIATSIS Library. Canberra: AIATSIS. 54 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only. Confirms Holmer 1966/1967 (B H748.91/A1, A2), Lissarrague 2007 (L D465.003/1), Widders 1979 (MS 3080, 'Open access - reading.. Not for Inter-Library Loan'; annotation: 'analyse phonology, word classes.. morphology and syntax'), Wafer & Lissarrague 2008 handbook; does not list the 2000 thesis or Embury 1976.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1966. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific Fascicle Five/Six. Anthropological Linguistics 8 (ERIC microfiche).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'Ngamba-Ngaku-Dainggati (Dangadi, Danggetti, Dhangatty, Thangatti..)' as Kuri subgroup item 4 only; the stress statement that the archive.org full-text search surfaced in this item ('the first vowel which is preceded by a consonant is stressed') is about Linngithigh, not Dhanggati.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Dhanggati language' (accessed 2026-09-17); PHOIBLE dyan1250 / inventory 2991; Glottolog dyan1250; muurrbay.org.au and dhanggati.org.au pages
sources.note: Wikipedia gives consonant/vowel inventory and vowel length but no stress statement; PHOIBLE gives a 19-segment inventory from 'Lissarrague nd'; Muurrbay and dhanggati.org.au pages give no pronunciation or stress notes and no PDFs.

sources.citation: Capell, A. 1970. Review of Holmer, An attempt towards a comparative grammar of two Australian languages, Part II, and other AIAS titles. AUMLA 33: 92-94.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes Kattang remnants at Purfleet, Thangatti at Kempsey/Bellbrook, and that phonemicisation is in Part I which was not submitted for review.

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1904. Ethnological notes on the Aboriginal tribes of New South Wales and Victoria. Journal and Proceedings of the Royal Society of New South Wales 38: 203-381 (section 'Language of the Thangatti tribe', pp. 232-235, plus vocabulary).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress or accent statement. The Thangatti sketch covers nouns, pronouns, verbs and numerals only; the only phonetic remark is that the language has a 'euphonic and flowing intonation' (p. 232). The general orthoepy note (pp. 205-207) applies to all languages in the treatise and says nothing about accent.

sources.note: The modern primary description of record (Glottolog's top grammar sketch; superseding Widders and Embury); Lissarrague's parallel Gathang grammar has an explicit stress section, so this one very likely states the Dhanggati stress rule in its phonology chapter.
